messages:
alex: Heads-up — noticed duplicated credit accrual after a reprocess of late billing events. Two shards accepted the same event_id during a backfill. @maria any ideas? :thinking:
Maria: ugh. seen similar when the handshake isn't strict. were the events stamped with provenance?
alex: yes, event had provenance: origin=proxy-12, attempt=2. But both consumer instances wrote a credit record.
jord: likely a race in the credit writer + no idempotency key check. We rely on event_id dedupe in the reconcile, but the writer is append-only.
sam: can we treat credit writes as upserts keyed by (customer_id, event_id)? that would make writes idempotent at storage layer.
Maria: upsert helps but we have sharded credit tables. event_id alone isn't enough for sharded key lookup. We'd need a canonical shard owner mapping or include shard_key=(account_id % N).
alex: current ingestion assigns shard by account_id mod N, but backfills sometimes set account_id to 0 for legacy records which makes collisions.
jord: two options: 1) normalize backfill events to real account_id before write, or 2) write a provenance marker and reject duplicates at writer by checking (event_id, provenance.site).
sam: option 2 is less invasive. writer can check a transaction: if exists(event_id) then no-op. But it adds an index and read-before-write. latency cost?
alex: rough numbers: our p99 for credit writes is ~12ms. doing a read adds ~6-8ms under load. for backfills it's fine; for steady-state bursty writes it might change SLOs.
Maria: could we batch dedupe at a coordinator? coordinator receives batch, dedup by event_id, then fan-out. That preserves write path latency for single events but delays them behind batch window. Not great for low-latency customers.
jord: another idea: use a monotonic sequencing service per account to give canonical sequence numbers. Then credit writes include seq_no and writers can accept only seq_no > stored_seq. But that's a big infra lift.
sam: Agree. Also we need to think about audit trail: any idempotency layer must keep an immutable audit log mapping attempts -> accepted events so audits can explain why a credit did/didn't apply.
alex: for immediate fix, propose: 1) add unique constraint on (event_id, account_id) in writer schema, 2) make backfill job normalize account_id, 3) deploy a lightweight dedupe read for steady-state writes behind a feature flag.
Maria: 👍 on the progressive approach. add a migration plan note: constraint enforcement with "deferred" flag then backfill cleanup window.
jord: small nit: ensure the unique constraint won't blow up when different provenance legitimately re-emits transformed events (e.g., transform pipeline changes token accounting). We need a transform_version field in the key.
sam: add transform_version to key + audit log entry with {event_id, transform_version, attempt_ts, ingest_node}.
ingest-bot: processed event 0x7f9c (event_id=ev_20260301_17, account=acct_42) -> wrote credit_row id=cr_98765 status=applied
alex: thanks. I'll sketch a PR for the writer constraint + feature flag and a small backfill normalizer. Will ping infra for migration window.
Maria: if you can include a quick perf test for read-before-write path that'd help decide rollout. Also add an entry in the metering runbook about late-arrival policy.
jord: can we also add an assertion in the audit reconciler to detect duplicate credits per event_id over a 30d window and emit a signal? helps catch regressions post-deploy.
sam: yes, create an alert "metering.duplicate_credit_rate" with low severity.
alex: cool. I'll open tickets: PR for writer change, migration playbook, reconciler assertion, perf harness. Assigning to myself and tagging @maria for migration ops.
Maria: thanks — will coordinate with platform ops for a quiet window. :thumbsup:
